docs.title: Mytoml
docs.text:
Mytoml is a lightweight TOML parsing and serialization library for C++17. It provides a small, type-safe API built on std::variant, std::map, and std::vector.

TOML 1.0 subset

Mytoml currently implements a line-oriented subset of TOML 1.0. Dates and times, multiline strings, quoted keys, arrays of tables, and inline comments are not supported. See the repository's REVIEW.md for the complete list of limitations.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
#include <mytoml/mytoml.hpp>

#include <iostream>
#include <string>

int main()
{
    const std::string text = R"(
title = "Mytoml"
enabled = true
retries = 3
ratio = 0.75
tags = ["toml", "cpp", "config"]

[server]
host = "127.0.0.1"
port = 8080

[server.limits]
timeout = 30
)";

    mytoml::toml config = mytoml::toml::parse(text);

    std::cout << config.as_table().at("title").as_string() << '\n';
    std::cout << config.as_table().at("server").as_table().at("port").as_integer() << '\n';
    std::cout << config.as_table().at("tags").as_array().size() << '\n';
}

Compile it directly against the library sources:

g++ main.cpp src/mytoml.cpp -std=c++17 -Iinclude -o main

Or build the bundled example with CMake:

cmake -S . -B build -DMYTOML_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON
cmake --build build --target Basic
./build/Basic

CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY is set to the top of the build tree, so example executables are placed directly in build/.

docs.title: Parsing
docs.text:
mytoml::toml::parse() takes a complete document as a std::string and returns a mytoml::toml value. A TOML document is a table at the root:

mytoml::toml document = mytoml::toml::parse(R"(
name = "demo"
values = [1, 2, 3]

[owner]
name = "Sackey"
)");

const mytoml::toml::table_t &root = document.as_table();

Supported syntax includes:

  • bare and dotted keys, such as server.port = 8080
  • table headers, including dotted headers such as [server.limits]
  • basic double-quoted strings
  • integers, floating-point numbers, and booleans
  • arrays, including nested arrays and inline tables
  • inline tables, such as meta = { name = "mytoml", stars = 5 }
  • full-line comments beginning with #

Unsupported constructs are described in REVIEW.md. Some unsupported values are silently stored as strings, so validate untrusted documents rather than assuming that parsing implies TOML compliance.

docs.title: Reading values
docs.text:
Each node exposes a type() query and a set of is_*() helpers:

mytoml::toml value = /* ... */;

switch (value.type())
{
case mytoml::node_t::table:
    // ...
    break;
case mytoml::node_t::array:
    // ...
    break;
case mytoml::node_t::string:
    std::cout << value.as_string() << '\n';
    break;
case mytoml::node_t::integer:
    std::cout << value.as_integer() << '\n';
    break;
case mytoml::node_t::floating:
    std::cout << value.as_floating() << '\n';
    break;
case mytoml::node_t::boolean:
    std::cout << std::boolalpha << value.as_boolean() << '\n';
    break;
default:
    break;
}

Use is_*() when the document is not trusted:

const auto &root = document.as_table();
const auto it = root.find("retries");

if (it != root.end() && it->second.is_integer())
{
    const int64_t retries = it->second.as_integer();
}

The accessors do not perform general conversions. as_floating() is the one exception: it returns an integer node converted to double. Calling an accessor for the wrong node type throws std::bad_variant_access, not a mytoml::exception.

docs.title: Navigating tables and arrays
docs.text:
Tables and arrays use standard containers, so the usual C++ iteration patterns apply:

const mytoml::toml::table_t &root = document.as_table();

for (const auto &entry : root)
{
    std::cout << entry.first << " = " << entry.second.type() << '\n';
}

const mytoml::toml::array_t &tags = root.at("tags").as_array();
for (const mytoml::toml &tag : tags)
{
    std::cout << tag.as_string() << '\n';
}

table_t is a std::map<std::string, toml>, so keys are sorted in the emitted document rather than preserved in input order.

docs.title: Modifying a document
docs.text:
Values can be inserted or replaced directly:

document.as_table()["enabled"] = false;
document.as_table()["retries"] = int64_t{5};
document.as_table()["release"] = "0.1.0";

Nested tables are built with toml::table_t:

mytoml::toml::table_t database;
database["url"] = "sqlite://demo.db";
database["pool_size"] = int64_t{4};

document.as_table()["database"] = std::move(database);

Arrays are built with toml::array_t:

mytoml::toml::array_t features;
features.emplace_back("parse");
features.emplace_back("emit");
document.as_table()["features"] = std::move(features);

docs.title: Emitting
docs.text:
dump() serializes a table as a TOML document. operator<< calls dump():

std::cout << document.dump();
std::cout << document; // equivalent

Top-level scalars are emitted before nested tables, and nested tables are emitted with [table] headers. An inline table is emitted with { key = value } syntax when it appears inside an array or another value:

mytoml::toml::array_t people;
mytoml::toml::table_t alice;
alice["name"] = "Alice";
alice["age"] = int64_t{30};
people.emplace_back(std::move(alice));

mytoml::toml output{mytoml::toml::table_t{{"people", mytoml::toml{std::move(people)}}}};
std::cout << output.dump();

Emitted strings are written verbatim; the current emitter does not escape quotes, backslashes, or control characters. See REVIEW.md.

docs.title: Literal operator
docs.text:
The _toml literal parses a string at run time:

using namespace mytoml::literals;

const mytoml::toml config = R"(
name = "from literal"
count = 2
)"_toml;

Literal operators are available for char, char8_t (when the compiler provides it), char16_t, and char32_t strings. The wide literal overloads currently truncate each code unit to a single byte and do not perform a full UTF conversion.

docs.title: Streams
docs.text:
operator>> parses from an input stream into an existing toml object:

std::istringstream input("answer = 42\n");
mytoml::toml config;
input >> config;

std::cout << config.as_table().at("answer").as_integer() << '\n';

The extraction operator takes const toml & for historical reasons and modifies the object through const_cast; prefer parse() in new code.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Errors raised by the library derive from mytoml::exception:

  • mytoml::parse_error for invalid documents
  • mytoml::encoding_error for encoding failures
  • mytoml::exception as the common base class
try
{
    mytoml::toml config = mytoml::toml::parse("key = \"unterminated");
    (void)config;
}
catch (const mytoml::parse_error &error)
{
    std::cerr << "parse error: " << error.what() << '\n';
}
catch (const mytoml::exception &error)
{
    std::cerr << "mytoml error: " << error.what() << '\n';
}

Many malformed values are currently accepted instead of rejected. For example, a value that is not a recognized number falls back to a bare string, and numeric conversion accepts a valid prefix such as 01abc. Validate input against your application's expectations and see REVIEW.md.

docs.title: Encoding helpers
docs.text:
Low-level UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32 helpers live in mytoml::detail:

const char check_mark[] = "\xE2\x9C\x93"; // U+2713

unsigned int codepoint = 0;
int consumed = mytoml::detail::utf8::decode(check_mark, sizeof(check_mark) - 1, codepoint);
if (consumed > 0)
{
    mytoml::detail::utf8::char_t buffer[4] = {};
    int written = mytoml::detail::utf8::encode(codepoint, buffer, sizeof(buffer));
    std::cout.write(reinterpret_cast<const char *>(buffer), written);
}

mytoml::detail::determine_encoding() recognizes byte-order marks for UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32. The parser itself does not strip BOMs or decode UTF-16/32 input; encoding conversion is currently available only through the helpers and the lexer.

docs.title: C API
docs.text: include/mytoml/mytoml.h currently provides the MYTOMLC_VERSION_* macros, the mtEncoding enum, and the mtVersion structure. It does not yet expose parsing or emission functions. Use the C++ API for now; the planned C API is described in IMPROVE.md.

docs.title: Testing and benchmarks
docs.text:
# Unit tests
cmake -S . -B build -DMYTOML_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build --target mytoml-cpp-tests mytoml-c-tests
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

# Micro-benchmarks
cmake -S . -B build -DMYTOML_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DMYTOML_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=ON
cmake --build build --target mytoml-cpp-benchmarks
./build/mytoml-cpp-benchmarks --benchmark-samples 10

The test suite uses Catch2, which is vendored under tests/vendor/Catch2. Benchmark targets are built separately and are not registered with CTest.
